label: Diagram 3.9
caption: Diagram 3.9 Common escape route in small single stair building
description:
The drawing is a plan, titled "Diagram 3.9 Common escape route in small single stair building", headed "See para 3.32", with two parts.

Part a, "Small single stair building", is a rectangular plan. A central lobby with a stair block on the right (shown with parallel step lines) opens to flats labelled "F" around the perimeter via doorsets labelled "Fd". A diagonal dimension across the lobby reads "4.5m max*". A wall on the right is marked "OV". A legend defines a green line as "Fire resisting construction", "OV" as "Openable vent at high level for fire service use (1.0m2 minimum free area); see paragraph 3.32e", "F" as "Flat" and "Fd" as "Fire doorset". A footnote states that if smoke control is provided in the lobby the travel distance can be increased to 7.5m maximum (see Diagram 3.7, example b).

Part b, "Small single stair building with no more than two flats per storey", is a smaller plan of the same arrangement. Text below notes the stair–lobby door should be free from security fastenings and that the lobby is not essential if flats have protected entrance halls.

Four NOTES appear at right: the arrangements also apply to the top storey; if the lobby travel in (a) exceeds 4.5m, Diagram 3.7 applies; where the lobby in (b) is omitted, an automatic opening vent of at least 1m2 is required at the top of the stair, operated on detection of smoke at any storey; and fire rating guidance is in Appendix C, Table C1.

notes: The description says part b "is a smaller plan of the same arrangement", but the drawing shows part b with only two flats (top and bottom) and a solid wall on the left side, whereas part a has flats and Fd doorsets on all four sides of the lobby, so the two plans are not the same arrangement.
